title: Research method for Blood pressure effector gene predictions (Kamali et al., 2022)
bodyHtml:
These results are from the study:

Large-Scale Multi-Omics Studies Provide New Insights into Blood Pressure Regulation.
Kamali Z, et al.
Int J Mol Sci. 2022 Jul 8;23(14):7557. doi: 10.3390/ijms23147557.
PMID: 35886906

In this analysis, candidate causal genes for diastolic blood pressure (DBP), systolic blood pressure (SBP) and pulse pressure (PP) were prioritized at genetically associated loci that were determined in a study of over a million individuals of European ancestry (Evangelou et al., 2018).

The contents of the table include:

  • Known vs. Novel: Novelty of the prioritized genes was assessed by lookups in the GWAS Catalog, Phenoscanner, and DisGeNET databases and in large-scale blood pressure meta-analyses (Evangelou et al., 2018; Giri et al., 2019)
  • Number of traits: Indicates the number of traits (DBP, SBP, or PP) providing biological evidence for a gene
  • Drug-Gene interactions: derived from the Drug Gene Interaction database (DGIdb)
  • DEPICT: "Yes" indicates that the gene is coregulated with other genes in BP GWAS loci more than expected by chance (FDR ≤ 0.01) in DEPICT analysis (Pers et al., 2015)
  • Coding variant: "Yes" indicates that the gene has a nonsynonymous coding variant(s) in LD (r2 > 0.5) with genome-wide significant BP associations
  • MetaXcan + colocalization: "Yes" indicates that the gene is significant in both MetaXcan (Barbeira et al., 2018) and colocalization analyses
  • SMR + HEIDI: "Yes" indicates that the gene is significant in both summary data-based Mendelian Randomization AND the HEterogeneity In Dependent Instruments test (HEIDI) (Zhu et al., 2016)
  • 3x SMR: "Yes" indicates that significant evidence resulted from all 3 summary data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR) runs: DNA methylation vs. BP (MSMR), DNA methlation vs. gene expression (MESMR), and gene expression vs. BP (ESMR).
  • Multi-layer associations: "Yes" indicates that based on Phenoscanner lookups, variants in the locus are associated with all 4 molecular traits (DNA methylation, gene expression, protein levels, and metabolite levels)
  • Systolic, Diastolic, and Pulse pressure analyses: "Yes" in a column indicates that biological evidence resulted from that trait
